title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: when free-time clocks start, stop and are counted
content:
## Scope

This policy of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category governs every free-time clock on a per-container record: which movements start and stop it, how its days are counted, which product governs it and which dates count as evidence.

## Counting clauses

1. Each clock starts the product's clock start offset after the calendar day of its start event and runs to the calendar day of its stop event, both counted.
2. So, where the offset is one day, the days used by a clock are the stop date less the start date, in calendar days.
3. Any part of a day counts as a whole day, and weekends and public holidays are counted.

In general terms, the days used by a clock are the number of calendar days from the start date to the stop date, less the offset, increased by one.

## Which clocks run

| Clock model | Record | Clock | Starts on | Stops on | Free days used |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| separate | import | demurrage | discharge date | full gate-out date | import demurrage free days |
| separate | import | detention | full gate-out date | empty return date | import detention free days |
| separate | export | detention | empty pickup date | full gate-in date | export detention free days |
| separate | export | demurrage | full gate-in date | loading date | export demurrage free days |
| combined | import | one merged clock | discharge date | empty return date | merged import free days |
| combined | export | one merged clock | empty pickup date | loading date | merged export free days |

## Governing product and evidence

4. The product in force on the record when the last clock stops governs every clock of the record, including days used before an upgrade.
5. Free time is judged on the dates the terminal and depot systems record; the customer's own account of a movement date never replaces a recorded date.

## Status effects

6. The record moves to charges accruing when any clock passes its free days while still running.
7. The record moves to clock stopped on the empty return of an import record or on the loading of an export record, and the clock-stop date is set to that date. It moves there from free time running when the last clock stops inside free time, and from charges accruing when it stops after free time has run out.

## Worked example (hypothetical dates, offset of one day)

An import container is discharged on 10 March and leaves full through the gate on 16 March. The first counted day is 11 March and the last is 16 March, so the demurrage clock has used 6 days: 16 March less 10 March.

## Wrong reading and correct basis

| Wrong reading | Correct basis |
|---|---|
| "The container was only out for part of the last day, so that day does not count." | Any part of a day counts as a whole day. |
| "The consignee says the box was returned on the 20th, so the 20th is the stop date." | Only the date the terminal or depot system records counts. |
| "Days used before the upgrade stay under the old product." | The product in force when the last clock stops governs every clock, including those earlier days. |
